title: Lindelöf gluing of the parametric co-area identity over countably many Borel pieces (parent steps 0(b), 0(c), 5)
statement:
Let n, N, m, k ∈ ℕ. Let D ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, Z ⊆ ℝⁿ arbitrary, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ continuous on D and injective on D, G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ continuous, and w : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] arbitrary.
Call a Borel set B ⊆ D good if, for every Borel φ : ℝᴺ → [0, ∞], the function y ↦ ∫_{ψ(B∩G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ is Lᵐ-a.e. measurable and ∫_B φ(ψ(u))·w(u) dLⁿ(u) = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{ψ(B∩G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ dLᵐ(y).
Assume:
- (Crit) every Borel B ⊆ D with B ⊆ Z is good;
- (Loc) every p ∈ D \ Z has an open neighbourhood O such that every Borel B ⊆ D ∩ O is good.
Then every Borel B ⊆ D is good.
Notation as in the parent: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hᵏ = μHE[k] (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Hausdorff outer measure); Lᵈ = volume.
